title: Use of the diagnostic PET with 64CuCl2 in order to select patients, in which a disease relapse is shown after prostate surgical removal, to be successfully treated to radiation therapy on the prostate bed.
official: Use of 64CuCl2 PET/CT Imaging in the selection of patients with prostate cancer in biochemical relapse after prostatectomy, to be successfully treated with salvage radiotherapy on the prostatic bed.
summary: Main objective: The primary objective is to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of PET with 64CuCl2 in the diagnosis of local recurrence of prostatic carcinoma after radical prostatectomy, in patients negative to traditional methods.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age>=45 years at the time of enrollment.
2. Previous execution mpMRI and/or US performance not older than 30 days.
3. Karnofski Index >= 80%
4. Absence of other relevant comorbidities (see: exclusion criteria).
5. Full ability to understand the information reported in the informed consent sheet.
6. Full ability to sign informed consent.
7. Previous documented histological diagnosis of primitive prostate adenocarcinoma.
8. Previous prior radical prostatectomy surgery.
9. Zeroing of circulating PSA values.
10. Presence of biochemical relapse documented by an increase in circulating PSA values in two consecutive determinations (values between 0.2 ng/ml and 1 ng/ml)
11. Absence of distant metastatic lesions not detectable by previous mpMRI and PET/CT imaging tests (18F-choline and/or PSMA).
12. Negative clinical history for other previous or current neoplastic diseases, with the exception of non-melanoma skin carcinomas.
13. Previous execution 18F-FCH PET and/or PSMA PET not older than 30 days.
14. Patients to be treated with salvage radiotherapy to the prostate bed.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Anemia with Hb <9 gr/dl
2. Major surgery performed in the previous 120 days.
3. Presence of lesions in the prostatic bed evidenced by previous mpMRI and/or US examinations.
4. Previous participation in clinical trials with exposure to ionizing radiation for therapeutic purposes.
5. Any condition, material, logistics, or Subjective, which, even in the opinion of the Principal Investigator, may condition the subject's compliance with the execution of the procedures established by the Protocol.
6. Inability to understand the contents of the information documentation for the subject.
7. Subject treated with ADT (orchiectomy, and/or LHRH agonists, and/or androgen antagonists).
8. Presence of symptoms or signs of sepsis and/or evidence of acute infections.
9. AST>1.5 times the upper limit of the normal range.
10. ALT>1.5 times the upper limit of the normal range.
11. Total bilirubin>1.5 times the upper limit of the normal range.
12. Copper metabolism diseases (Menkes’ disease, Wilson’s disease).
13. Subjects who have received chemotherapy in the previous 120 days.
14. Radiotherapy performed in the previous 120 days.
